newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ACCC not troubled by bank/insurance mergers.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ACCC not troubled by bank/insurance mergers.

text.p: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) chairman Allan Fels said on Friday that the regulatory body still believed there would be few competition concerns with a merger of a large bank and insurance company.
"That is unlikely to be a problem," Fels told reporters, referring to a possible merger after the Wallis Inquiry report is handed down in the near future.
Currently the "six pillars" policy of the national government prevents a merger between Australia's four major private banks and the two leading insurance companies.

Fels said the ACCC, when it was the Trade Practices Commission, examined the prospect of a merger between Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) and National Mutual Holdings Ltd in the early 1990s.
The ACCC approved the merger, ruling that the insurance and banking markets were separate and that the merger would not unduly hurt competition.
But the merger was prevented by the then Labor government, who instituted the "six pillars" policy in response to public concern about concentration of ownership in the financial sector.
"There's probably no problem about insurance and banking getting together as far as mergers are concerned," Fels said.
Fels said whatever was decided after the Wallis report, the ACCC would examine each merger proposal under its merits and would look at the situation again.

He said structural changes were happening in the financial services sector, referring to increasing convergence between the sectors and possibility of insurance groups being granted access to the payments system currently available to the banks only.
So the ACCC would look at each proposal at the time it was made, leaving open the possibility the bank and insurance markets may be significantly more blurred than in the ANZ-NMH case.
The Wallis Inquiry into the Financial Services sector is due to report to the government by the end of March and make recommendations on the sector.
The inquiry is widely expected to recommend the end of the "six pillars" policy and recommend the government hand over authority to reject or accept mergers to the ACCC.
